title: [Chapitre] IV. Analysis situs (première mouture) : notes manuscrites (10/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting, from the surrounding pages: M is a poset of 'multistructures' or 'multiplicités', ordered by ≤ (sub-multistructure). Below each X the poset M_{≤X} is apparently finite. L is a set of elements x (the 'lines', or fine elements). There is an incidence or 'smallness' relation x << X, and L_X = {x ∈ L : x << X} is the line refining X. The program, stated on p.20, is to reconstruct the structures << and compatibility on M from the set-valued maps X ↦ L_X.

On this page:
(1) The map M_{≤X} → P(L), X_i ↦ L_{X_i}, is increasing. If X_j ≤ X_i, then x << X_j implies x << X_i, so L_{X_j} ⊂ L_{X_i}.
(2) Grothendieck wants it strictly increasing: X_j < X_i should give L_{X_j} ⊊ L_{X_i}. That means there is an x with x << X_i and not x << X_j.
(3) He defines the 'open part' L°_X = L_X \ ∪_{X_i<X} L_{X_i} and states a stronger condition (Cond./Conj. 3): for every X ∈ M, L°_X ≠ ∅. In words, some x is incident to X but to no proper sub-multistructure of X.
(4) Claim: for X ∈ M, L_X = ∪_{X_i ≤ X} L°_{X_i}. Proof: given x ∈ L_X, the set of X_i ≤ X with x ∈ L_{X_i} is non-empty (it contains X). Since M_{≤X} is finite, this set has a minimal element X_i, and then x ∈ L°_{X_i}.

The next page continues: x ∈ L°_{X_i} iff X_i is minimal among such Y. Grothendieck wants this minimal element to be unique, which makes L_X the disjoint union of the strata L°_{X_i}. This becomes Conj. 4 (disjointness for distinct compatible X, Y). Its equivalent form, noted in the margin, is L_X ∩ L_Y = ∪_{Z≤X, Z≤Y} L_Z.

In modern terms, he is axiomatising a stratification or cell decomposition indexed by a poset. Each 'closed cell' L_X is the union of 'open cells' L°_Y for Y ≤ X. Open cells are non-empty, and he wants them disjoint, as for the face poset of a regular CW complex or a stratified space. This sits within the 1986 'Analysis situs' project of a combinatorial or tame foundation for topology.
errors: The parenthetical writes 'X_j << X_i dans L_{X_j} ⊂ L_{X_i}'. The meaning is 'X_j ≤ X_i ⇒ (x << X_j ⇒ x << X_i) donc L_{X_j} ⊂ L_{X_i}'. This tacitly requires << to be compatible with ≤ (transitivity), which is assumed but not stated here.
The existence of a minimal X_i relies on M_{≤X} being finite (or at least well-founded). This is only implicitly justified on the next page ('X fini').

Cond. 3 is strictly stronger than strict monotonicity. Strictness needs, for each Y < X, some element of L_X outside L_Y. Cond. 3 needs a single element avoiding all L_Y for Y < X at once. Grothendieck notes it is 'plus forte', so this is correct, not an error.

ideas.what: Open part L°_X = L_X minus the union of L_Y over Y<X, with the non-emptiness condition
ideas.modern_name: Open cells/strata of a poset-indexed stratification (frontier condition, non-empty open cells)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical: CW complexes (Whitehead) and stratifications (Whitney, Thom)
ideas.where_published: Tame topology is only sketched in Esquisse d'un programme (1984), §5–6, without this formalism

ideas.what: Decomposition of the closed cell L_X as the union of the open cells L°_Y for Y ≤ X, via minimal elements in a finite poset
ideas.modern_name: Closure of a stratum is a union of strata (frontier condition)

ideas.what: Program of reconstructing incidence and compatibility structure on M from the set-valued map X ↦ L_X
ideas.modern_name: Recovering a poset or cell structure from its representation by sets (face-poset / Alexandrov-type reconstruction)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Alexandrov (finite spaces); face posets of regular CW complexes (Björner etc.)

missed.claim: Grothendieck sets up an axiomatic incidence calculus (multistructures, lines, <<) aimed at a combinatorial analysis situs. He states conditions/conjectures (Cond./Conj. 3: open parts non-empty; Conj. 4 on the next page: disjointness of open parts for compatible multistructures). These amount to requiring that the multistructures form a regular-cell-like stratification of the lines. The fate of these conjectures within his framework is not settled on this page.
missed.quote: Soit L°_X = L_X \ ∪_{X_i<X} L_{X_i}. Condition plus forte ... ∀X ∈ M, L°_X ≠ ∅
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is of mainly historical interest. It documents the 1986 unpublished attempt at a combinatorial/tame topology foundation linked to Esquisse §5. The mathematics on this page itself is elementary.

deep.surprise_reason: This is an elementary poset/stratification argument inside an unpublished axiomatic project. It has historical interest for the 1986 Analysis situs program, but there is no new mathematical result here.
transcription_corrections: The crossed-out first line is likely 'Soit X une multistructure' (crossed out), consistent with p.20, rather than 'multiplicité'.
In the parenthesis, 'dans' should be read as 'donc': '... ⇒ x << X_j ⇒ x << X_i, donc L_{X_j} ⊂ L_{X_i}'.
The margin label read as 'Cond 3' is probably 'Conj 3' (or 'Cond 3'), parallel to 'Conj 4' on p.22.
In the final displayed condition, the second clause reads 'x ≪̸ X_i pour les X_i < X'.
Insertion above 'réunion': '(qui est ⊂ L_X)', with the underlined word 'égale'.
The crossed-out line near the bottom: 'et les X_i [forment un ouvert de] M_{≤X}'.
